company: Cromwell Property Group (Cromwell Corporation Limited and Cromwell Property Securities Limited)
title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors and employees
tiers.description: All Cromwell directors and senior management and employees. The policy applies identically to directors and employees throughout: same closed periods, same clearance requirement from a Disclosure Officer, same hedging and margin loan prohibitions.

tiers.name: Disclosure Officer
tiers.description: Each of the Company Secretary, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Executive Officer. Grants or refuses clearance to deal, may declare additional closed periods, and decides whether exceptional circumstances exist for a sale-only clearance during a closed period.

tiers.name: Associated persons
tiers.description: Nominees, agents, family members, family companies or family trusts of a director or employee; any investment manager acting on their behalf or on behalf of such an associated person; and any people or entities over which the director or employee may exert influence in investment decisions.

definitions.hedging_definition: an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading lock, forfeiture condition, restriction period or other restriction in a Group employee security scheme

windows.start_anchor: 60 days immediately preceding the announcement of the Group's preliminary final report (usually 1 July), or if shorter, the end of Cromwell's financial year (30 June)
windows.end_anchor: announcement of the Group's preliminary final report (usually 31 August)

windows.start_anchor: 60 days immediately preceding the announcement of the Group's half-year report (usually 1 January), or if shorter, the end of Cromwell's half year (31 December)
windows.end_anchor: announcement of the Group's half-year report (usually 28 February)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: A Disclosure Officer may declare any other closed period (paragraph 7(a)(iii)), or a closed period relating to the securities of another listed entity about which Cromwell has obtained inside information (paragraph 7(b)), by emailing affected directors and employees in advance. Directors and employees may be asked to keep the details of any such closed period confidential.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. Group Securities includes options and any other financial product issued or created over or in respect of Group Securities, with no venue limit, and Dealing includes granting, exercising or discharging an option or other right over securities, so an OTC put/call is a Dealing requiring prior written clearance from a Disclosure Officer, barred in closed periods and while holding inside information.
rules.evidence: any other financial products issued or created over or in respect of Cromwell Property Group securities (ASX:CMW) traded on the ASX.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on any arrangement limiting exposure to risk on unvested remuneration, reaffirmed at paragraph 19(a) which overrides the general 'dealing not covered' exceptions for unvested employee security scheme entitlements.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees are prohibited from entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested

rules.detail: The same ban extends to vested securities that remain subject to a trading lock, forfeiture condition, restriction period or other restriction in a Group employee security scheme, not just unvested holdings.
rules.evidence: or which remains subject to a trading lock, forfeiture condition, restriction period or other restriction in a Group employee security scheme.

rules.detail: Hedging of fully vested, unrestricted holdings is not named in paragraph 13; it is caught only as an ordinary Dealing (a financial product created in respect of Group Securities) requiring Disclosure Officer clearance and compliance with closed periods.
rules.evidence: any other financial products issued or created over or in respect of Cromwell Property Group securities (ASX:CMW) traded on the ASX.

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. a prepaid forward) is not named. An agreement to dispose of securities is a Dealing requiring Disclosure Officer clearance and compliance with closed periods.
rules.evidence: entering into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere, and stock borrowing (needed to effect a short sale) is also not addressed.
Securities lending is not named and is not listed in the Dealing definition.
CFDs are not named. As a financial product created in respect of Group Securities they are a Dealing requiring Disclosure Officer clearance and compliance with closed periods.
rules.evidence: any other financial products issued or created over or in respect of Cromwell Property Group securities (ASX:CMW) traded on the ASX.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on margin lending arrangements narrowly defined as those where security rights over Group Securities are granted to a third party and are exercisable based on actual or potential changes in the value of the Group Securities. The policy expressly confirms this does not extend to other secured loan arrangements.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees are prohibited from entering into margin lending arrangements under which security rights over Group Securities are granted to a third party and are exercisable based on actual or potential changes in the value of the Group Securities.

rules.detail: Only margin-lending-type security rights (exercisable on value-based triggers) are banned. Other loan arrangements secured by a security interest granted in respect of Group Securities are expressly not caught by the section 14 prohibition, though granting the security would still be assessed against the general Dealing/clearance regime.
rules.evidence: This prohibition includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Group Securities.

rules.detail: Secured financing other than margin lending in the strict sense is expressly permitted; entering into it would still need to be assessed for Disclosure Officer clearance as a Dealing and comply with closed periods and the inside information bar.
rules.evidence: does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Group Securities.

rules.detail: Selling Group Securities within 30 days or less of acquisition is not allowed, subject to the paragraph 19 carve-outs (DRP issues and proper administration of/participation in an employee security scheme).
rules.evidence: Short term trading of Group Securities (i.e. selling Group Securities within 30 days or less from the date of acquisition) is not allowed.

clearance.approver: a Disclosure Officer (Company Secretary, Chief Financial Officer or Chief Executive Officer)
clearance.post_trade_to: the Disclosure Officer who provided the clearance
clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified ('when the dealing has in fact occurred')
clearance.evidence: Before dealing in Group Securities, a Cromwell director or an employee must first inform a Disclosure Officer in writing of the intention to trade and seek clearance.

short_term.basis: 30 days or less from the date of acquisition
carve_outs: any proper issue of Group Securities under a Cromwell distribution reinvestment plan
any dealing as a result of the proper administration of, or participation in, an employee security scheme
short_term.evidence: Short term trading of Group Securities (i.e. selling Group Securities within 30 days or less from the date of acquisition) is not allowed.

exceptions.evidence: any proper issue of Group Securities under a Cromwell distribution reinvestment plan
any dealing as a result of the proper administration of, or participation in, an employee security scheme

that results in no change in beneficial interest in Group Securities including any transfer of Group Securities already held by a director or employee, or by a company that they control or by a super fund, family trust or similar scheme
any dealing in Group Securities by a fund, scheme or arrangement (other than one that only invests in Group Securities) where investment decisions are made at the discretion of a third party.
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, an announced takeover offer.
any dealing under an offer or invitation made to all or most Group securityholders such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan and an equal access buy-back

exceptions.approver: other trustees or an investment manager acting independently
exceptions.evidence: where a director or employee is a trustee, trading in Group Securities by that trust provided the director or employee is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision made during a closed period ... is made by the other trustees or by an investment manager independently of the director or employee.

The Disclosure Officer may give clearance for a director or an employee to sell (but not buy) Group Securities in exceptional circumstances where the director or employee would otherwise not be able to do so under this Policy. For example, if the director or employee has a pressing financial commitment that cannot otherwise be satisfied.

external_documents: Group employee security scheme rules (referenced in paragraphs 13 and 19(a))
exemption_authority: The Disclosure Officer may grant or refuse clearance to deal, and may give a sale-only clearance during a closed period in Exceptional Circumstances (e.g. a pressing financial commitment), which the Disclosure Officer alone decides is exceptional (paragraph 9); clearance can never be given, under either the general or exceptional-circumstances route, if there is a matter about which there is inside information (paragraphs 8(b)(i), 9(d)).

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin loan carve-out for other secured loans
bespoke_clauses.clause: This prohibition includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Group Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The section 14 ban targets only classic margin lending with value-triggered security rights; a bank's fixed-collateral loan secured on the collared shares is not 'properly described as a margin lending arrangement' and so falls outside the prohibition, though it must still be cleared as a Dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees are prohibited from entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading lock, forfeiture condition, restriction period or other restriction in a Group employee security scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar cannot be written over unvested remuneration or vested shares still subject to a trading lock or other scheme restriction; only fully vested, unrestricted holdings can be the reference security.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a director or an employee may not deal in the Group Securities, they must prohibit any dealing in the Group Securities by any associated person ... or any investment manager on their behalf
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the individual is restricted (closed period or inside information), the collar cannot be executed through a spouse, family trust or discretionary investment manager on their behalf during that period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Disclosure Officer may give clearance for a director or an employee to sell (but not buy) Group Securities in exceptional circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only discretionary relief from a closed period is a sale-only clearance for pressing financial need; there is no equivalent route to write a call or buy a put during a closed period, so collar entry must occur in an open window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees may be asked to keep as confidential the details of any such closed period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Cromwell can impose undisclosed extra closed periods, including ones triggered by inside information about another listed entity, creating execution timing risk that cannot be explained to the bank while confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An employee who deals in securities should use only one broker. Employees may not use broker credit.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Financing for the collar cannot be structured as broker credit; it must come through a separate facility such as a bank loan, reinforcing reliance on the section 14 carve-out for non-margin secured loans.

summary: A funded collar is achievable under this policy for a director or employee holding fully vested, unrestricted Cromwell securities. The OTC put and call are Dealings caught only via the Group Securities/dealing definitions (options and other financial products issued or created in respect of Group Securities), so they require prior written clearance from a Disclosure Officer (Company Secretary, CFO or CEO), must be entered outside the 60-day pre-results closed periods and any other Disclosure-Officer-declared closed period, and cannot proceed while the individual holds inside information. Section 14 prohibits only margin lending arrangements in the strict sense - security rights exercisable on changes in the shares' value - and expressly states this does not extend to other loan arrangements secured by a security interest over Group Securities, so a fixed-collateral loan securing a collar is not banned, though creating it would still need Disclosure Officer clearance as a Dealing. The collar cannot be written over unvested remuneration or shares still subject to a trading lock, forfeiture condition or other scheme restriction, since any hedge over such securities is absolutely prohibited with no exception. Associated persons and discretionary investment managers must be kept from dealing whenever the individual is themselves restricted, and the only closed-period relief available is a discretionary sale-only clearance for pressing financial commitments, so entry into new put/call positions must occur in an open trading window.
